title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
authors: Colin Raffel, Noam Shazeer, Adam Roberts, Katherine Lee, Sharan Narang, Michael Matena, Yanqi Zhou, Wei Li, Peter J. Liu
date: October 2019 (arXiv v1 23 October 2019; JMLR 2020; arXiv v4 September 2023)

live.text: run the objectives on your own text

takeaway: Casts every NLP task as text in, text out so that objective, architecture, corpus, fine-tuning scheme and multi-task mixing become swappable ablations of one fixed pipeline: encoder-decoder plus span corruption wins, denoising beats language modelling while the denoising variants barely differ, unfiltered Common Crawl is worst everywhere despite being 8x larger, and multi-task pretraining then fine-tuning matches plain pretraining; scaled to 11B on 1T tokens of the new C4 corpus for 90.3 GLUE and 88.9 SuperGLUE against a human 89.8, though translation stayed out of reach on English-only pretraining.

kb.n: 2017: the encoder-decoder T5 keeps, with three changes (rescale-only norm, norm outside the residual path, relative position bias).
2018: T5's denoising objective is a modified BERT masked LM, and the architecture ablation is largely a controlled test of BERT's encoder-only assumption.
2020, seven months later and pointing the other way: in-context learning on a decoder-only stack instead of fine-tuning; the two papers together are the fork in the road.
2021: built directly on this setup, T5-Base and T5-Large on C4 with span corruption as the dense control, and up to 7x faster pretraining against them.
2022: T5's scaling section asks the same question (more compute: size or steps?) informally at a fixed 4x budget; Chinchilla answers it with a fitted law.
2020, contemporaneous: the counterpoint on knowledge, facts in a swappable index rather than in the weights T5 scaled up.
2025: encoder-only against decoder-only with one recipe at matched sizes; finds the split task-dependent.
2025 to 2026: decoder-only Gemma adapted into an encoder-decoder; the closest modern rerun of T5's encoder-decoder against decoder-only result.
2020: loss as a power law in parameters, data and compute; the fitted version of T5's "bigger model or more steps" question.

topics.n: pretraining objectives, multi-task mixing, transfer learning.
where the frozen T5 encoder lives on, as the text conditioner of Imagen, Stable Diffusion 3 and FLUX.1.

verdict: Believe the big gaps (denoising over language modelling, an encoder-decoder over a causal LM, cleaned over unfiltered web text, pretraining over multi-task training alone): they are 8 to 42 standard deviations of the paper’s own run-to-run noise. Read its many “no difference” findings as “none detectable with one run each at 220M”, not as proof of equality.
